bug.title: Report a bug
bug.intro: Your message goes to the D2Vita maintainer. Before writing, check that the problem is not already listed in the [known issues](https://github.com/Franckrst/D2Vita/issues).
bug.rail.crash.title: Did the game crash?
bug.rail.crash.body: On the next launch, D2Vita offers to send a crash report with the technical details. This form is still useful to describe what you were doing.
bug.field.title.label: Title
bug.field.title.hint: One sentence that sums up the problem.
bug.field.description.label: Description
bug.field.description.hint: What you were doing, what happened, and whether it happens again.
bug.field.version.label: D2Vita version
bug.field.lang.label: Language of your message
bug.field.lang.hint: The language you are writing in.
bug.field.contact.label: Contact
bug.field.contact.hint: Email or username, if you are happy to be contacted.
bug.turnstile.label: Bot check
bug.turnstile.unavailable: The bot check could not load. If a content blocker is active, allow challenges.cloudflare.com, then reload the page.
bug.error.required.title: Enter a title.
bug.error.turnstileMissing: Complete the bot check before sending.
bug.error.invalid: The server rejected the form. Check the fields, then try again.
bug.error.turnstile: The bot check failed or expired. Complete it again, then resend the form.
bug.error.forbidden: The server refused the request. Try again later.
bug.error.rateLimited: Today’s sending limit has been reached. Try again {when}.
bug.error.rateLimitedLater: Today’s sending limit has been reached. Try again later.
bug.error.server: The report service isn’t responding correctly. Try again later.
bug.error.network: Couldn’t reach the report service. Check your connection, then try again.
bug.note: The form sends these fields and the bot-check token. [What happens to them](privacy.html#bugs)
bug.success.title: Report sent
bug.success.body: Thank you. Keep its ID: it lets the maintainer find your report if you refer to it later.
page.privacy.title: Privacy — D2Vita
page.privacy.description: What D2Vita crash reports contain, how consent works, how long data is kept and how to have it deleted.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: D2Vita can send crash reports to its maintainer, and this site lets you report a bug. Here is what is collected, when, and how long it is kept.
privacy.glance.title: At a glance
privacy.glance.consent: **Nothing is sent without your consent.** After a crash, the console asks you first.
privacy.glance.sealed: **Attachments are encrypted on the console.** Only the maintainer can read them.
privacy.glance.secrets: **Your CD keys and account name are not sent:** they are scrubbed from logs, and a dump that contains them is held back.
privacy.glance.ip: **Your IP address is never stored in clear.**
privacy.glance.delete: **You can have your reports deleted** using the [installation ID](#deletion) shown by the console.
privacy.toc.title: On this page
privacy.when.title: When a report is offered
privacy.when.p1: On the launch after a crash, D2Vita looks for traces of the previous session: a PS Vita system dump, the `Crash.txt` file written by the game, a fault recorded in its logs, an abnormal exit or a freeze.
privacy.when.p2: If it finds no trace, nothing is offered or sent. That is normally the case when the game is simply closed with the PS button.
privacy.when.p3: A freeze can be a false alarm, for example if the game stayed in the background before being closed. The message says so, and you decide.
privacy.choice.title: Your choice
privacy.choice.intro: Before anything is sent, the console shows a message that summarises the report and offers three answers:
privacy.choice.send: **✕ Send:** the report is sent while the game starts.
privacy.choice.decline: **○ Don’t send:** pending reports are deleted from the console.
privacy.choice.always: **△ Always send without asking:** the choice is saved in `ux0:data/d2vita/reports/consent.txt`. Delete that file, or add the line `D2_CRASHREPORT=ask` to `ux0:data/d2vita/env.txt`, to be asked again.
privacy.choice.later: With no answer after 60 seconds, you will be asked again later. The same report is offered three times at most, and no pending report is kept for more than seven days.
privacy.choice.off: To turn everything off, collection included, add the line `D2_CRASHREPORT=0` to `env.txt`.
privacy.choice.scripted: When the console is driven by a test script (`D2SCRIPT` or `D2CMDFILE`), no message is shown and reports stay pending.
privacy.choice.installId: The installation ID is shown in small print under the message. Write it down if you might want your reports deleted one day.
privacy.claim.title: What the summary contains
privacy.claim.intro: Every accepted report starts with a summary of 16 KiB at most. It is sent unencrypted and contains:
privacy.claim.reportId.desc: Generated by the console, so the same report is never counted twice.
privacy.claim.installId.desc: A 128-bit random number drawn on first launch and saved in `ux0:data/d2vita/reports/install_id.txt`. It has no link to your account.
privacy.claim.build.desc: The exact D2Vita version and its release channel (`release`, `dev` or `test`).
privacy.claim.platform.desc: The model and firmware version, when the application can read them.
privacy.claim.session.desc: Launch time, session length, and whether the game was online.
privacy.claim.kind.desc: Application crash, game stopped on an error, fault in the game code, abnormal exit or freeze. Other traces found are attached as hints.
privacy.claim.features.desc: Depending on the type: error code and location, crash addresses (in the form `Game+0x1fedf4`), the thread involved and why it stopped.
privacy.claim.artifacts.desc: The name and size of the attachments ready to send, and how many replacements the scrubbing made, never the values found.
privacy.claim.headers: Console requests also carry the D2Vita version and the installation ID in their headers. The summary contains no account name, no CD key and no IP address.
privacy.attach.title: Attachments
privacy.attach.intro: If this type of error is already known, the summary is enough: the service adds one to a counter and asks for nothing else. If it is new, it asks for a single copy of the attachments below.
privacy.attach.col.name: Attachment
privacy.attach.dump.name: System dump
privacy.attach.dump.content: The `psp2core` file the PS Vita creates when the application crashes, unmodified. It contains part of the application’s memory at the time of the crash.
privacy.attach.crashTxt.name: `Crash.txt`
privacy.attach.crashTxt.content: The error report written by the game.
privacy.attach.crashTxt.when: Game stopped on an error, abnormal exit
privacy.attach.crashLog.name: `crash.log`
privacy.attach.progress.name: `boot_progress.txt`
privacy.attach.progress.content: D2Vita’s activity log: its beginning, its end, and the lines around a fault.
privacy.attach.resample: A new copy can be requested when the maintainer asks for one, or when a problem marked as fixed comes back.
privacy.attach.outbox: Until they are sent, these copies stay on the console in `ux0:data/d2vita/reports/outbox/`: five reports and 4 MiB at most, oldest deleted first.
privacy.redact.title: What is scrubbed before sending
privacy.redact.p1: Before sending, the console searches the attachments for your Diablo II and Lord of Destruction CD keys (read from `ux0:data/d2vita_secret/keys.txt`, with or without dashes, in upper or lower case), the owner name stored in that file, and the last Battle.net account name remembered by the game.
privacy.redact.p2: In the logs, each occurrence is replaced with `X` characters of the same length. If one of them appears in the system dump, the dump is not sent: only the logs are.
privacy.redact.p3: These search patterns are built at startup, kept in memory only, then erased.
privacy.crypto.title: Encryption and transport
privacy.crypto.sealed: Attachments are encrypted on the console with the maintainer’s public key, built into D2Vita (X25519 and XChaCha20-Poly1305). The private key never leaves the maintainer’s computer: neither Cloudflare, which hosts the service, nor GitHub, nor anyone watching the network can read them.
privacy.crypto.http: The console sends its requests over plain HTTP, without TLS, because the encrypted connections the host requires are not reliably available on the PS Vita. The summary therefore travels unencrypted, which is why it contains nothing that names you.
privacy.crypto.signed: The service’s responses are signed and the console checks the signature: a third party on the network cannot trigger uploads or block reports by pretending to be the service.
privacy.server.title: What the service keeps, and for how long
privacy.server.host: The report service runs on Cloudflare (Workers, D1 database, R2 storage). The maintainer reads it from their own computer with an admin token.
privacy.server.dedup: For each error type, the service keeps an occurrence counter, the list of affected versions and the number of distinct consoles. To count consoles, it derives a pseudonym from the installation ID (HMAC with a secret key).
privacy.server.ip: Your IP address is used to limit how much can be sent: the service only keeps a fingerprint of it (HMAC with a salt that changes every day), never the address in clear.
privacy.retention.heading: Retention
privacy.retention.reports.desc: Deleted after 180 days. Only aggregated counters remain.
privacy.retention.artifacts.desc: Not deleted automatically while the problem is open; deleted 90 days after it is marked fixed or ignored.
privacy.issues.title: Public issues
privacy.issues.p1: The maintainer can open a public GitHub issue for an error type. The draft only includes aggregated information: error type, number of occurrences and consoles, affected versions, first and last seen dates, crash addresses. Never the logs or the dump. It is reviewed before publication.
privacy.bugs.title: The bug report form
privacy.bugs.sent: The [Report a bug](bug.html) form sends, over HTTPS, the title, the description, the version, the contact if you give one, the chosen language and the bot-check token.
privacy.bugs.turnstile: The bot check is Cloudflare Turnstile. Its script is loaded from `challenges.cloudflare.com`, only on the form page.
privacy.bugs.limits: Your IP address is also used, as the same kind of fingerprint, to limit the number of bug reports per day.
privacy.bugs.public: The maintainer may turn a bug into a public GitHub issue: don’t write anything in the title or description that you would not want published.
privacy.site.title: This site
privacy.site.p1: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages. It reads no crash data and uses no analytics. It only remembers your chosen language, in your browser’s local storage.
privacy.delete.title: Having your data deleted
privacy.delete.p1: Each installation has an ID, shown in small print under the report message and saved in `ux0:data/d2vita/reports/install_id.txt`.
privacy.delete.p2: To have the summaries and attachments linked to your installation erased, send that ID with the [Report a bug](bug.html) form, with “Delete my data” as the title.
privacy.delete.p3: To stop sending anything in the future, answer “Don’t send”, or add the line `D2_CRASHREPORT=0` to `env.txt`.
